decisive_items: facial features included a thick head of hair, bushy eyebrows, a short upturned philtrum, a high nasal bridge with a beak-shaped nose
response.rationale: Cohen syndrome is strongly supported by the combination of intellectual disability, transient neutropenia, microcephaly, truncal obesity, joint hyperextensibility, high myopia, and characteristic facial dysmorphism, all present in this patient.

rejected.why: Alström syndrome lacks neutropenia and characteristic facial dysmorphism; typically presents with hearing loss and cardiomyopathy, which are absent.
Bardet-Biedl syndrome typically presents with polydactyly and renal anomalies, which are absent; also lacks the specific facial features and neutropenia.
